lenders.name: Farmers & Merchants Bank of Long Beach
lenders.footprint: California state-chartered bank headquartered in Long Beach
lenders.programs: Portfolio multifamily residential loans (balances reported in its call reports); no published product terms
lenders.broker_program: None found. No multifamily product page, broker page or referral program surfaced in searches (wave 1 also found none). Approach through the bank's commercial real estate lending team.
lenders.fit_notes: Long Beach bank with a multifamily residential loan book tracked in its call reports (RC-C data at 12/31/2025). Useful for Southern California apartment deals, but no product terms or broker channel are published.

lenders.name: Poppy Bank
lenders.footprint: California (branches listed in Walnut Creek, Fremont, Los Altos, Costa Mesa and Beverly Hills chamber directories)
lenders.property_types: Multifamily, Commercial real estate, Construction, Skilled nursing / senior housing (bridge)
lenders.programs: Commercial real estate, Construction, SBA / USDA loans, Multifamily portfolio loans, Healthcare (SNF) bridge loans
lenders.broker_program: No broker page found. Evidence it takes intermediary-arranged deals: Berkadia announced in June 2024 that it worked with Poppy Bank to close 12 SNF bridge loans totaling over $329.7M. That evidence is healthcare, not apartments.
lenders.fit_notes: California community bank with about $728.5M of multifamily residential loans at year-end 2025 (call report). It has closed broker-arranged healthcare bridge loans, so ask whether its CRE team takes broker multifamily submissions.

lenders.name: Citizens Business Bank
lenders.parent_or_aka: CVB Financial Corp. subsidiary; call reports filed as Citizens Business Bank, National Association
lenders.programs: Portfolio multifamily loans (balances reported in call reports); no published product terms
lenders.broker_program: None found. One search returned only call-report data; most results were for the unrelated Citizens Bank (Citizens Financial Group).
lenders.fit_notes: California bank with about $836.4M of multifamily loans on its call report. Product terms and broker policy were not found, so treat as a relationship-bank lead.

lenders.name: Logix Federal Credit Union - Commercial Real Estate
lenders.footprint: Southern California credit union (Valencia HQ); also sells CRE loan participations to other credit unions
lenders.property_types: Multifamily, Office, Retail, Light industrial, Light manufacturing
lenders.programs: Commercial real estate term loans (purchase and refinance), CRE loan participations sold to credit unions
lenders.max_leverage: Up to 70% on a new purchase
lenders.broker_program: No broker program found on its business lending pages. Credit union lending may require membership; ask the commercial lending team.
lenders.fit_notes: SoCal credit union whose CRE page lists multifamily and advertises up to 70% purchase financing. Job postings show an active multifamily underwriting team. Broker acceptance is unconfirmed.

lenders.name: ClearEdge Lending
lenders.programs: DSCR 5-8 unit / 2-8 unit mixed-use investor loans (wholesale)
lenders.broker_program: Wholesale lender: its site has a broker 'Price Your Loan' pricing page listing a '5-8 Units/2-8 Mixed Use' DSCR product, and a March 2024 broker flyer for the 5-8 unit program (loans up to $2M, reserves as low as 9 months, experienced investors).
lenders.fit_notes: Wholesale channel for very small apartment buildings (5-8 units) that agency and bank lenders often skip. The flyer is from March 2024 and California eligibility is unconfirmed, so get the current matrix from an account executive.

lenders.name: Lendmarq
lenders.parent_or_aka: Resfin Partners platform (with correspondent arm Eastview); Castlelake took majority ownership in April 2026; Leste Group remains an investor
lenders.programs: Fix & flip, Bridge, Ground-up construction, DSCR rental; Castlelake's purchased pool included multifamily bridge loans
lenders.broker_program: Trade press describes Lendmarq as a direct lender to investors that works with brokers, with white-label funding that keeps the broker's branding in front. No broker terms or sign-up page found.
lenders.fit_notes: Mostly a residential-investor lender; multifamily bridge is a small part of its output. Castlelake's April 2026 majority stake and a 2026 RMBS outlet give it fresh capital. HQ is given as West Palm Beach in one profile and Miami in others; California lending unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Harper Capital Partners
lenders.programs: HUD 223(f) acquisition / refinance, HUD-insured healthcare loans, HUD permanent takeout of bridge loans
lenders.speed_to_close: Under 5 months on a $56M HUD 223(f) purchase (2020 release)
lenders.broker_program: None published. Its CEO has said buyers often use bridge financing first and then bring deals to Harper for a HUD takeout.
lenders.licenses: FHA/HUD-approved mortgage lender (per its 2020 releases); MAP status not confirmed in search
lenders.fit_notes: Specialist HUD multifamily and healthcare lender that says it has worked on more than $5B of transactions. Evidence is from 2020; confirm current activity, MAP approval and California deals.

lenders.name: Highland Commercial Mortgage
lenders.property_types: Multifamily, Affordable housing, Senior living, Healthcare
lenders.programs: HUD 221(d)(4) new construction, FHA multifamily, Affordable housing, Senior living / healthcare FHA loans
lenders.broker_program: None published.
lenders.licenses: FHA MAP and LEAN approved (directory listing); 'FHA, MAP approved lender' per its June 2026 release
lenders.fit_notes: Active FHA MAP lender: in June 2026 it announced HUD 221(d)(4) financing for a 270-unit Class A community in Orlando (president Chip Moore). Deals found are in the Southeast; broker channel and California lending unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Enterprise Bank & Trust - SBA Lending
lenders.parent_or_aka: Enterprise Financial Services Corp (NASDAQ: EFSC); absorbed Seacoast Commerce Bank's San Diego SBA business (2020 acquisition)
lenders.footprint: Multi-state bank; SBA operations in San Diego, CA (former Seacoast Commerce team)
lenders.programs: SBA 7(a), SBA 504, SBA construction loans
lenders.broker_program: No broker or referral program found. Its SBA team is in San Diego (SBA servicing, construction processor and business development roles posted there).
lenders.fit_notes: Surviving brand of Seacoast Commerce Bank (excluded in wave 1 as acquired). Its site has a hotel case study (Shree Hospitality) where it used an SBA 504 loan. Caveat: in October 2025 it disclosed seven Southern California CRE loans totaling $68.4M in foreclosure.

lenders.name: Plumas Bank - SBA Lending
lenders.footprint: Northern California and Nevada (Reno HQ; Sacramento SBA / CRE loan office)
lenders.programs: SBA 7(a), Commercial real estate
lenders.broker_program: No broker program found.
lenders.fit_notes: Northern California SBA lender: SBA data shows 429 SBA 7(a) loans totaling $334.4M from FY2020 to Q1 FY2026 (average about $780K), including two Motel 6 loans. Hotels are a side line; its SBA team focuses on business acquisitions.

lenders.name: Leader Bank - SBA Referral Partner Program
lenders.programs: SBA 7(a) loans
lenders.broker_program: Documented referral program aimed at mortgage brokers: pays referral fees on funded SBA loans ($250K-$5M), offers a free SBA training academy, a direct line to its team and a written referral agreement. Fees are disclosed on SBA Form 159.
lenders.fit_notes: One of the few SBA lenders with a written broker-pay program. Hotel appetite and California lending were not confirmed; SBA lender roles are posted in several markets, including LA.

lenders.name: First Utah Bank - Hospitality Lending
lenders.footprint: Utah-based bank; hotel lending area not stated
lenders.programs: Hotel ground-up construction, Acquisition, Expansion, Renovation, Refinance, SBA 504, SBA 7(a), USDA, Equipment financing, Sale-leaseback
lenders.broker_program: None published. Its hospitality page presents the bank as a one-stop shop for hotel construction and acquisition loans plus treasury management.
lenders.fit_notes: Bank with a dedicated hotel lending page claiming over $100M of hotel projects funded since 2014 (another section says over $114M). Fits small hotel construction and SBA deals, but its lending area is unconfirmed and likely Mountain West.

lenders.name: American Bank, N.A. (Dallas) - Hospitality Lending
lenders.parent_or_aka: American Bank, N.A.; bought in 2019 by investors tied to hotel company NewcrestImage
lenders.footprint: Dallas-Fort Worth bank; hotel lending area not stated
lenders.programs: Conventional hotel loans, SBA 7(a), SBA 504, Commercial lines of credit
lenders.broker_program: None published.
lenders.fit_notes: Small hotelier-owned bank with a dedicated hospitality lending page. Its examples include a $5.3M hotel CRE acquisition and a $3.24M SBA hotel refinance. California lending unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Siguler Guff - Credit & Special Situations (real estate lending)
lenders.footprint: National (deals found in CA and TX)
lenders.programs: Bridge loans, Mezzanine loans
lenders.broker_program: No published broker page. Intermediary evidence: in July 2025 its Credit & Special Situations team led a $13.9M bridge loan, announced by Thomas Financial Group, on two historic Sierra foothill hotels (National Exchange Hotel, Nevada City; Holbrooke Hotel, Grass Valley), to be taken out by a $14.3M USDA B&I loan. In Sept 2025 it closed an $11M mezz loan on Waco, TX apartments alongside a $23M Benefit Street Partners senior loan.
lenders.fit_notes: Private credit lender with a recent California hotel bridge loan under $15M on an intermediary-led deal, used as bridge-to-USDA. Thomas Financial Group (already in the directory) is the proven route in.

lenders.name: American Plus Bank
lenders.footprint: San Gabriel Valley, CA community bank
lenders.property_types: Hospitality (hotels/motels), Multifamily, Retail (shopping centers), Office / medical, Industrial / warehouse
lenders.programs: CRE purchase and refinance loans, SBA loans (real estate, equipment, refinance, tenant improvements)
lenders.broker_program: None published.
lenders.fit_notes: Arcadia community bank whose commercial loan page names hotels/motels among CRE purchase and refinance collateral, and which also offers SBA loans. A third-party aggregator puts recorded mortgage volume at about $98.8M over 12 months (average $2.3M). Hotel-SBA deals and broker acceptance unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Preferred Bank - SBA Lending
lenders.programs: SBA 7(a) (uses include real estate purchase, leasehold improvements and construction)
lenders.broker_program: None published. Its SBA page gives a desk email for inquiries.
lenders.fit_notes: Other desk of Preferred Bank. LA-based SBA 7(a) desk whose listed uses (real estate purchase, construction) cover hotel deals, but no hotel-specific SBA program or deal was found. Ask the SBA desk about hotel appetite and Form 159 referral fees.

lenders.name: Golden Bank, N.A.
lenders.footprint: Texas and California: branches in Tustin, Alhambra, Rowland Heights, Cupertino, Fremont and Millbrae, plus an Irvine loan production office
lenders.programs: SBA 7(a), Commercial real estate
lenders.broker_program: None found.
lenders.fit_notes: Houston Asian-American bank with six California branches and an Irvine LPO. SBA data shows 136 SBA 7(a) loans totaling $192.8M from FY2020 to Q1 FY2026 (average $1.4M). Hotel lending and broker acceptance unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Eagle Realty Group (Western & Southern Financial Group commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Western & Southern Financial Group; Eagle Realty Group is its real estate investment subsidiary
lenders.property_types: Commercial real estate (property-type parameters on its site were not captured)
lenders.programs: Commercial mortgage loans, Mezzanine, Equity joint ventures
lenders.broker_program: No correspondent list or broker program found. Eagle originates, underwrites and places debt, equity and mezzanine capital on a direct and joint-venture basis for Western & Southern and its affiliated insurers. Its mortgage-loans page describes its lending process.
lenders.fit_notes: Life-company balance-sheet lender with a published mortgage-loans program page. Commercial mortgages are a small slice of Western & Southern Life's portfolio (about $56.9M of $11.5B invested assets in 2021, parent-company statutory filing). California activity and broker acceptance unconfirmed.

lenders.name: Guardian Life Insurance Company of America (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America; subsidiary Guardian Insurance & Annuity Co. (GIAC) also holds a commercial mortgage book
lenders.programs: Fixed-rate permanent commercial mortgage loans (10-yr fixed example)
lenders.broker_program: No correspondent list or broker program found. No intermediary was named on the California deal found.
lenders.fit_notes: California deal found: a $55M 10-year fixed loan to Prime Residential on Paz Mar Reserve, a waterfront apartment community in Oxnard (date not confirmed). GIAC's filings show California was its largest concentration (about 21% of commercial loans at YE2024) but no new GIAC originations in 2025. Deals found are above Corin's sweet spot.

lenders.name: AuguStar Life Insurance Company (formerly Ohio National Life) - commercial mortgage loans
lenders.parent_or_aka: Constellation Insurance; Ohio National Life Insurance Company is the recorded lending entity
lenders.property_types: Multifamily, Office, Stabilized commercial real estate
lenders.programs: Fixed-rate permanent commercial mortgage loans on stabilized properties
lenders.broker_program: No correspondent list or broker program found.
lenders.fit_notes: Life company that makes small loans: average origination was about $2.5M (2017-2018 filings), and a third-party profile cites fixed-rate loans from $1M to over $10M on stabilized multifamily and office. Commercial mortgage book about $1.06B at YE2021. California lending and the intake channel (correspondents?) unconfirmed.

lenders.name: American Equity Investment Life Insurance Company (commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: American Equity Investment Life Holding Co.; ownership changed in 2024 (Brookfield acquisition; not re-verified in this search)
lenders.programs: Commercial mortgage loans (program started 2001)
lenders.broker_program: No broker or correspondent channel found in filings.
lenders.fit_notes: Life company commercial mortgage program with small average loans ($4.7M at Sept 2020). The Pacific region (which includes California) held 19.0% of principal at March 2021. Evidence is 2020-2021 SEC filings; confirm the program is still active after the ownership change.

lenders.name: Aegon Asset Management - Aegon Real Assets US (Transamerica commercial mortgage loans)
lenders.parent_or_aka: Aegon Ltd.; originates commercial mortgage loans for Transamerica and unaffiliated insurance clients
lenders.property_types: Multifamily, Industrial, Other commercial property types
lenders.programs: Fixed-rate permanent commercial mortgage loans, Construction-to-permanent loans
lenders.broker_program: No correspondent list or broker program found in search. Aegon describes in-house origination and servicing for affiliated and unaffiliated life insurers.
lenders.fit_notes: Life-company lender sized for mid-market deals: typical loan about $15M, range $3M-$50M depending on the insurer client; average origination $12.6M at 12/31/2023. It has cut loan size for a client that wanted smaller multifamily and industrial loans. California activity and intake channel unconfirmed.

lenders.name: KEB Hana LA Financial / Hana Bank USA
lenders.parent_or_aka: Hana Financial Group (Korea); KEB Hana LA Financial makes the loans, Hana Bank USA, N.A. takes deposits (LA branch opened Aug 2025)
lenders.footprint: Los Angeles (lending affiliate); Hana Bank USA plans West Coast growth
lenders.property_types: Commercial real estate, Owner-occupied CRE, Multifamily, Hospitality (hotels)
lenders.programs: Commercial mortgage loans (CML), Corporate lending, Trade finance; Hana Bank USA profile lists SBA, owner-occupied CRE, multifamily and C&I loans
lenders.broker_program: None found.
lenders.fit_notes: Korean bank group's LA lending arm offering commercial mortgage loans. A KEB Hana entity lent $21M on a Koreatown hotel (May 2020), though the exact entity is unconfirmed. SBA hotel activity and broker acceptance unconfirmed.
